newsitem.title: USA: Rubin hails first index-linked debt sale.
newsitem.headline: Rubin hails first index-linked debt sale.

text.p: Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin hailed the results of the U.S. government's first auction on Wednesday of index-linked debt, saying it had resulted in a fair price for both buyers and the seller.
"They (the notes) went very successfully," he told public television's Nightly Business Report program.
The $7 billion sale of 10-year inflation-indexed notes, carrying a coupon interest rate of 3.375 percent, drew strong bidding that resulted in a high yield rate of 3.449 percent.
"I think this rate is a very fair rate, both for the buyers and the seller," Rubin said.
Much of the demand for the notes came from financial institutions, although there was some retail buying interest as well, Rubin said.
He said it was too soon to say how much money the Treasury will save American taxpayers by selling index-linked debt, but added that it was clear there will be some savings.
He indicated that the Treasury's next sale of index-linked debt in April was likely to be another 10-year note, although he made clear that eventually other maturities would be sold.

"We have to decide what we want to do with the next issue," he said. "We could issue additional ten years, which I think might be a very sensible thing to do. But at some point, we will issue these same securities in a different maturity."
The Treasury Department plans to sell inflation-indexed debt four times a year.
